summary: Implemented the durable lifecycle fence, the disable/uninstall drain and guarded restoration, the supported image-removal primitive, and confirmed item-removal tombstoning in src/ArrTags/Artwork and src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle (ADR-002/ADR-003; docs/architecture.md section 9; docs/data-model.md sections 3.10.1-3.10.4), then applied the independent-review corrections F1/F2/F3 and the task-critical test additions F5. ArtworkLifecycleFenceRecord is the versioned authoritative record and ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore its store: the active Normal/Disable/Uninstall/ItemRemoved fence is integrity-tagged, atomically written, normal when absent, and fail-closed when invalid. StateRepository gained a bounded deterministic Enumerate scan and PluginStatePaths a kind-directory accessor so the coordinator can list durable operations and states without a Jellyfin item listing. ArtworkPublisher reads the durable fence before accepting new work, refuses it unless the fence is a valid Normal, and records the fence on the operation it creates. The publisher also gained RestoreAsync, a guarded restoration that reuses the same durable Prepared -> MutationStarted -> RepositoryUpdateStarted -> VerificationPending -> FinalizationPending -> Committed ordering, immediate before-mutation revalidation, and readback postcondition commit as publication: a present retained source is written through the supported stream SaveImage API, an absent baseline is removed through the new IArtworkImageWriter.RemoveImageAsync, and a surface that does not match the retained baseline enters RecoveryBlocked/RestoreBlocked with no further automatic mutation. JellyfinArtworkImageWriter.RemoveImageAsync uses the supported BaseItem.DeleteImageAsync flow (local file removal when local, image-info removal, and the normal ItemUpdateType.ImageUpdate repository update) and never deletes a media file or image-cache entry directly; all MediaBrowser.* references stay confined to that single implementation file. ArtworkRecoveryDecisions.Evaluate gained an optional active-fence argument and ArtworkReconciler a matching ReconcileAsync overload, so a disable/uninstall drain aborts an in-flight prepared publication (AbortFenced) instead of resuming it, and the publisher recovery path now executes a restoration resume instead of reporting Deferred. ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator (IArtworkLifecycleCoordinator) records the fence, reconciles every non-terminal operation to a terminal result before creating the guarded restoration, restores every still-owned Published surface, leaves the active image and all recovery records in place and reports Incomplete when a restoration is blocked, externally changed, or uncertain, treats a recovery-blocked operation as incomplete, and tombstones a confirmed item removal with no Jellyfin image call. Correction F1: the drain classifies each reconciled operation by the durable operation phase rather than by the transient reconciliation outcome, so an operation that becomes RecoveryBlocked (for example through an OwnershipUnknown or non-throwing source-read failure) is never counted as resolved and the lifecycle result is Incomplete. Correction F2: ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore reads an invalid/corrupt fence without quarantining it away and Reset never overwrites it with Normal, so the publisher read path stays fail-closed until an explicit recovery decision. Correction F3: the item-removal path only claims a tombstone after the reconciler actually aborted the in-flight operation, and returns Blocked with tombstoned:false when the reconciler cannot reach the ItemRemoved decision (for example an invalid/quarantined state or operation). ArrTagsLifecycleService clears a stale valid fence on StartAsync when the host loaded the plugin active, performs a bounded DrainForHostShutdownAsync plus tracked item-removal confirmations on StopAsync (a plain shutdown resolves Normal and is a no-op), and wires the previously no-op ItemRemoved hint to a tracked bounded task so synchronous library event delivery is never blocked. IPluginLifecycleFenceProvider is the host-neutral fence source and JellyfinPluginLifecycleState its single Jellyfin implementation, mapping the persisted plugin manifest status through the supported IPluginManager. Plugin.OnUninstalling records the Uninstall fence and performs a bounded synchronous drain because the pinned host deletes the plugin data folder immediately after the hook; it resolves the coordinator lazily, never throws into the host, and leaves a blocked or uncertain restoration untouched. All new services use the existing lazy DI factory pattern with no startup work, and no source artifact or journal record is deleted eagerly.

known_limitations: There is no Jellyfin OnDisable hook. The chosen disable trigger is the persisted plugin manifest status read through the supported IPluginManager during the graceful StopAsync of the still-loaded instance; a disable that is only observed after the plugin has been unloaded (for example a disable followed by a hard kill without a graceful shutdown) is not detectable from inside the plugin. The durable fence still prevents new publication work while it is present. This boundary is documented in docs/architecture.md section 9.

The pinned Jellyfin host deletes the plugin data folder (which equals the plugin install folder) immediately after the synchronous Plugin.OnUninstalling hook returns. The hook therefore performs a bounded synchronous drain (GetAwaiter().GetResult with the 15 second BoundedDrainTimeout) because that is the only point at which the retained source artifact and journal are still present. If the drain times out or a restoration is blocked, ArrTags leaves the image and records untouched but the host may still delete the folder; ArrTags itself never deletes the source artifact or journal. This is the smallest faithful trigger and is documented.

An invalid or corrupt durable lifecycle fence is preserved and never overwritten with Normal by the automatic startup reset, so the publication read path stays fail-closed. Clearing such a fence requires an explicit recovery decision that this task intentionally does not perform; until then new publication remains refused. This is the fail-closed behavior requested by reviewer correction F2.

A blocked, externally changed, or uncertain restoration writes a terminal RestoreBlocked state and a RecoveryBlocked/Aborted operation and is reported as an incomplete lifecycle result; it is not automatically retried, consistent with the design that an uncertain restoration does not perform another automatic mutation. Explicit administrative re-baseline remains out of scope.

No eager plugin-owned artifact cleanup is implemented. A tombstoned or restored operation is terminal and becomes eligible for the existing StateRepository retention policy; artifact-byte cleanup and full retention wiring remain Phase 6, and no artifact is deleted that is not proven non-active.

No live-host, native-Skia, or package-content validation was performed for this task; the host lifecycle wiring, the image-removal ABI call, and the DI graph are exercised with injectable doubles and no real Jellyfin library is mutated. A live-host disable/uninstall/restore validation remains part of the later acceptance/gate work.

The Plugin constructor gained an IServiceProvider parameter resolved by Jellyfin's ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance so the uninstall hook can resolve the coordinator lazily without a startup dependency; the existing foundation tests use GetUninitializedObject and remain valid.

The broader library-event/queue/enqueue/scheduled-scan/caching/invalidation pipeline (Phase 6), Enhanced coexistence (5.10), and route/client tests (5.11) are intentionally not implemented; only the minimal ItemRemoved tombstone handling and the host lifecycle fence triggers required by task 5.9 were added.
